title: Guide - Healing and Hope - God is near

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Healing and Hope. <short pause> This practice is called God Is Near. <short pause> Whatever has broken, and however long ago it broke, you can bring it here. <short pause> You don't have to explain it first.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself be held up by the chair, or the floor, or whatever is beneath you. <short pause> If some part of you is hurting, there's no need to force it to relax. <short pause> Just give it a little room. <short pause> Breathe in as far as is comfortable... <short pause> and let the breath go.

When we are in pain, it can seem that God must be somewhere else. <short pause> With the people who are singing, perhaps. <short pause> The people whose prayers were answered. <short pause> But when you can't feel Him, it doesn't mean that He has left you. <short pause> Pain can fill a room so completely... that it's hard to see who is sitting beside us.

Long ago, God spoke to a people who had lost a great deal, and were afraid of what was still to come. <short pause> He didn't tell them there would be no deep water. <short pause> He told them who would be in it with them. <short pause> It is written in Isaiah forty-three, verse two.
When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: When you pass through. <short pause> Not around. <short pause> Not high above, on some bridge for stronger people. <short pause> Through. <short pause> And there, with the water cold against you, and the far bank out of sight... <short pause> I will be with thee.

What are the waters for you, just now? <short pause> A diagnosis? <short pause> An ending you didn't choose? <short pause> A slow recovery that others have stopped asking about? <short pause> You don't need to wade any deeper to answer. <short pause> From where you stand, simply name it to Him... <short pause> this is my water, Lord.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now rest one hand in the other, if you are able. <short pause> Feel the warmth where they meet. <short pause> Let it remind you of a hand you cannot see. <short pause> As you breathe in, hear Him say... I will be with thee. <short pause> As you breathe out, answer with as little as you have... here I am. <short pause> And again... I will be with thee. <short pause> Here I am.

A child being carried across a stream doesn't have to know how deep it is. <short pause> She doesn't have to find the stones with her feet. <short pause> She may even cry the whole way over. <short pause> It changes nothing about the arms that are carrying her.

So if your grip is weak today, that is all right. <short pause> Your safety was never in how tightly you could hold on. <short pause> He is near when you feel it, and near when you don't. <short pause> And sometimes His nearness has a human face... a nurse, a friend, someone who sits down and stays. <short pause> You are allowed to let them.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, You see the water I am standing in. <short pause> I don't ask to understand it all. <short pause> I ask You to be close. <short pause> When I cannot feel You, keep hold of me still. <short pause> Bring me kind hands, and give me the humility to take them. <short pause> Amen.
Carry four words with you from here. <short pause> I will be... with thee. <short pause> Say them at the edge of whatever comes next. <short pause> Go gently. <short pause> You do not cross alone.
